Subject: MAP kickoff: Performance evaluation plan & timelines

Emma —

Thanks for the time today. As discussed, I put together a draft Mutual Action Plan focused on the performance evaluation we’ll run across Hosted, Dedicated and Private (on-prem/VPC) modes. The goal is twofold: 1) validate predictability and isolation characteristics for your peak concurrency patterns, and 2) produce an apples-to-apples cost/latency profile to inform the procurement decision.

High-level scope (attached: FinTechX_MAP_v1.xlsx):
- Metrics: P95 latency, mean latency, throughput (tokens/sec), time-to-first-token (TTFT), memory/KV cache pressure, error rates during autoscale events.
- Scenarios: baseline (low concurrency), ramp (linear to target concurrency), spike (10x short duration), sustained high-concurrency (8 hours), noisy-neighbor isolation test for Dedicated vs Private.
- Envs: Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), Private (VPC deployment with customer network).
- Success criteria: P95 < 300ms for typical prompts at 4k context in Dedicated, TTFT < 200ms for short prompts, predictable throughput within ±15% of baseline for Dedicated/Private during autoscale window.

Proposed timeline:
- Aug 19: exchange final prompt sets and dataset (you)
- Aug 21–22: Redwood run baseline & ramp tests (Hosted + Dedicated)
- Aug 23: Private deployment smoke tests (with your infra team)
- Aug 24: Full spike & sustained tests, run isolation scenarios
- Aug 25: results review and commercial alignment (pricing/commit)

Action items for FinTechX: share final prompt set + representative concurrency profile (peak RPS) and identify an ops contact for Private/VPC network setup.

I’m looping in Rishi (technical lead) and Jonas (dedicated capacity) for the test definitions and resource scheduling.

Adding technical notes and test config specifics so we have a reproducible plan: (see attached perf-test-config.yml)

Test definitions (concise):
- Baseline: 1–4 concurrent sessions, 8 prompts/session, verify P95 and TTFT at 4k tokens.
- Ramp: linear increase to target concurrency (provided by FinTechX) over 30 minutes; measure autoscale latency, queue length, and token throughput.
- Spike: sudden 10x RPS for 2 minutes followed by recovery; capture error rates and KV cache eviction metrics.
- Sustained-high: run at target concurrency for 8 hours to observe thermal throttling and GPU memory fragmentation.
- Isolation: on Dedicated, launch co-located synthetic jobs to saturate PCI-E and measure latency tail; on Private, run the same with the customer's NIC interruption script to validate network resilience.

Data collection hooks: token-level timestamps, GPU utilization, nvlink counters, process OOM logs (if any), and Redwood runtime tracing (link in related_links).

Notes: for Hosted tests we'll simulate customer RPS but throttling/fallback policies may engage — we'll capture those events and mark them in the results.

Subject: Results & close plan: Aug 24 test outcomes + recommended next steps

Team —

Summary of runs completed today (full logs and dashboards linked in related_links):
- Hosted (simulated peak of 120 concurrent sessions): P95 latency 420ms on long prompts, TTFT averaged 310ms; autoscale kick-in latency observed at ~45s; noticeable tail variability during spike.
- Dedicated (reserved 4xA100 pool): P95 latency 260ms, TTFT 180ms, throughput consistent within ±8% of baseline during sustained-high. No runtime OOMs; KV cache hit-rate 92%.
- Private (customer VPC, same instance types): P95 latency 270ms, TTFT 190ms, but we saw a transient NIC packet drop during the 10x spike that resulted in 1.4% error rate — traced to a tuning parameter on the customer's side.
- Isolation tests: Dedicated showed strong isolation (tail stable); Hosted had higher variance under co-located synthetic load as expected.

Conclusions & recommended close steps:
1) Dedicated meets your predictability and isolation SLOs.
2) Private provides parity in latency but requires a brief network hardening window (we’ll share a checklist).
3) Hosted is cost-effective for non-critical traffic but shows tail variance for bursty peaks — recommend hybrid routing (Dedicated for peak-critical routes).

Proposed immediate next actions (for Aug 25 pricing review and sign):
- FinTechX to confirm target committed qps and preferred capacity ladder (emailed by Emma).
- Redwood to produce a Dedicated pricing & commitment letter (Marissa) + a short SOW for onsite Private hardening (Rishi/Jonas).
- Schedule a 60-min signoff call Aug 25 10:00 PT.

Emma — happy to jump on a quick call now if you want to talk through the NIC finding; otherwise we’ll review tomorrow and capture final commercial terms.

Jonas Weber
